note: Track minor-colours, step 1: harmonic minor, natural minor with a raised 7th, tapped against natural minor on two staffs, over a drone, then as the ending of the learner's own tunes in a second key, with a line that says what stays. The key is moves (any key): the old Key selector is gone, the key is named as {{=key}}, and each section has a feel to reach.

exercise.title: Harmonic minor: the raised 7th
exercise.why: Harmonic minor is natural minor with the 7th raised a half step, so the 7th sits right under the root and leads up to it.

cells.text: Tap {{5}}, the ringed {{b7}} and the {{1}} above them on the staff below: {{=key}} natural minor, with a whole step from {{b7}} up to {{1}}.

Now tap {{5}}, the ringed {{7}} and {{1}} on this staff: {{=key}} harmonic minor. {{7}} is a half step under {{1}}.
Practice until you can hum the raised note before you tap it.

Press Play below to start the drone on {{=key}}. Tap {{1}}, the ringed {{7}} and {{1}} on the staff under it, then tap the whole scale from {{1}} up to the next {{1}} and back down.
Listen for the wide step between {{b6}} and {{7}}.
Practice until that wide step sounds like part of the scale, not a mistake.

Press Play below to start the drone, in a new key a 5th higher. Tap short tunes of your own on the staff under it, and end each one on the ringed {{7}} and then {{1}}.
Practice until that ending sounds like home.
In the new key the notes are new, and {{7}} is still a half step under the root.
